## Why visit

An excellent choice when the group wants good beer and a meal together rather than treating food as a separate logistical task. The former tailor’s premises now contain two contrasting floors with an intimate, characterful feel. Cask, cider and tapas give it a clear reason to be included beyond its location in the Village. Use it as a meal anchor near Piccadilly or as a change of atmosphere after the small Portland Street pubs; it contributes a distinct part of Manchester’s pub culture.

## Beer

Four handpumps are documented, not necessarily all in use, with local beer and varied craft styles.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA explicitly flags real cider and lists Celtic Marches; ask which current product qualifies.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Fresh tapas with vegetarian/vegan choices documented. A strong meal candidate.

## Plan the visit

The operator says Saturday is walk-ins only. Check kitchen times separately and reserve on other days if making dinner the anchor.

**Getting there:** Walk from Manchester Piccadilly or Piccadilly Gardens; near Circus Tavern and Grey Horse.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
